These instructions guide GitHub Copilot in BudgetWise: a .NET 8 ASP.NET Core Web API with React TypeScript/Vite/Tailwind frontend for personal-finance training.

**Code:** Follow standard C# naming (PascalCase types/methods/properties; camelCase locals/parameters), meaningful names, focused concise methods (single responsibility), composition over inheritance, C# 12 where appropriate, `var` when obvious, and `using` inside namespaces. Use TypeScript with strict checking; React hooks/functional components, focused reusable components, Tailwind utilities (avoid inline styles), semantic HTML, accessibility (ARIA and keyboard navigation). Use constructor dependency injection and appropriate Scoped/Singleton/Transient lifetimes. Consistently use minimal APIs or controllers; REST nouns/HTTP verbs; typed results or `IActionResult`; Data Annotations; built-in middleware; separate record DTOs; explicit domain/DTO mapping; camelCase JSON; Content-Type headers. Add XML docs to public classes/methods with `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, and applicable `<exception>`; comments explain WHY, .NET/React concepts; mark incomplete work `// TODO:` plus a clear description.

**Testing/API/data:** Use xUnit and React Testing Library; AAA; descriptive names `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult`; `WebApplicationFactory<T>` integration tests; mock external dependencies; test success, failure, edge/boundary cases, interactions (not implementation), accessibility, and `screen` queries; mock APIs with MSW or similar. Use GET/POST/PUT/DELETE appropriately and status codes 200/201/404/400; plural endpoints (`/api/expenses`), IDs (`/api/expenses/{id}`), filters (`/api/expenses?category=Food`); validate with Data Annotations or FluentValidation; meaningful errors. Use in-memory collections for development/testing; populate realistic representative data through `MockData` in `Data/MockData.cs`; thread-safe collections where necessary; property-based model initialization; navigation properties; nullable references (`?`); `required` for mandatory C# 11+ properties.

Follow existing patterns first; ASP.NET conventions; existing React/TypeScript style; error handling/validation; tests alongside implementation; XML docs and JSDoc; client-side form validation; typed responses/statuses; frontend/backend coherence. Implement TODOs using existing patterns, write tests, update documentation, prioritize clarity over cleverness, keep code beginner-friendly, and demonstrate best practices. Some features are intentionally marked `// TODO` for workshop exercises.

❌ Do not use service locator pattern (always use dependency injection)
❌ Do not return null from API endpoints (use `NotFound()` or throw exceptions)
❌ Do not put business logic in controllers (use services)
❌ Do not ignore exceptions or use empty catch blocks
❌ Do not use `any` type in TypeScript (use proper types or `unknown`)
❌ Do not create side effects in React component render functions

**Paths:** `budgetwise-app/backend/Program.cs` is entry point/middleware; `budgetwise-app/backend/Controllers/` endpoints; `budgetwise-app/backend/Models/` models/DTOs; `budgetwise-app/backend/Services/` business logic; `budgetwise-app/backend/Data/MockData.cs` mock data; `budgetwise-app/frontend/src/App.tsx` app; `budgetwise-app/frontend/src/services/api.ts` client; `budgetwise-app/frontend/src/types/index.ts` types; `budgetwise-app/README.md` documentation.

cd budgetwise-app/backend
dotnet restore              # Restore dependencies
dotnet build                # Build the project
dotnet run                  # Start the API server (port 5000)
dotnet test                 # Run tests
dotnet watch run            # Run with hot reload
cd budgetwise-app/frontend
npm install                 # Install dependencies
npm run dev                 # Start dev server with Vite (port 5173)
npm run build               # Production build
npm run preview             # Preview production build
npm run lint                # Run ESLint
npm ru
